channel.title: Los Angeles Review of Books – Reviews
channel.description: Book reviews from the Los Angeles Review of Books.

item.title: Murky Effects
item.description: A novel of desire and domestic disorder amid a disintegrating literary establishment.

item.title: The Queen of Hearts
item.description: A newly translated biography of Virginia Oldoini, Countess of Castiglione, aims to reveal the real woman behind the subject of everyone’s gaze.

item.title: Scatological Graffiti and Other Arts
item.description: A critical overview of the field of classics, and a memoir of a half century studying antiquity.

item.title: Nonpredictive Texts
item.description: Exploring ‘DTF St. Louis’ and the anti-algorithmic worlds of Steven Conrad.

item.title: Who Is Supreme, the People or the Court?
item.description: Nikolas Bowie and Daphna Renan’s new book challenges the supremacy of judicial review over democracy itself.

item.title: California Sons: Miriam Pawel’s “The Browns of California”
item.description: Jake Wertz reviews “The Browns of California,” a four-generation biography of the Brown family and a portrait of the state they shaped.

item.title: A Flamboyant, Impatient Rebel
item.description: Tom Overton’s biography of John Berger blends the meticulous archival research we expect from a professional historian with the subjective and intimate familiarity of the memoirist.

item.title: I Was a Child, and They Ate My Heart
item.description: Fady Joudah’s newest poetry collection resists the idiomatic “unspeakable” when faced with evidence of the ongoing genocide in Gaza.

item.title: The Slow Apocalypse of Capitalist Decay
item.description: Hernan Diaz completes his hopeful trilogy following the rise and fall of American capitalism.

item.title: Locked in the Drawer of Devotion
item.description: Jake Rose’s new poetry collection transports Joan of Arc from the 15th century to today.

item.title: Another Means to Torment
item.description: Alma Katsu crafts beauty horror for the age of influencers.

item.title: We Tell Ourselves Dinosaur Stories in Order to Live
item.description: We live within a library of antediluvian narratives, with more accessioned every day.

item.title: The Impression of Living in a Ruin
item.description: Spanish author Elvira Navarro’s newly translated story collection captures the unease, decay, and isolation of our post-pandemic world.

item.title: Free Verse, Late Fame
item.description: Kent Jones’s film ‘Late Fame’ preaches the necessity of art while also decrying society’s escalating attempts to use it as a means of profit and power.
